title: Slicer: Prusa CORE One L shows Clone Profiles dialog (false-negative + 'col1' template bug)
description:
After selecting "Prusa CORE One L" (and likely other Prusa CORE One variants) in the slicer machine selector, the Clone Profiles dialog appears with the message "No machine profiles found" — even though Prusa profiles DO exist in the OrcaSlicer profile bundle (machine_list/machine_model_list entries for Prusa CORE One, Prusa CORE One L, Prusa CORE One HF, Prusa CORE One L HF) and the manifest lookup succeeds (cover image and bed STL/texture render correctly).

Two distinct bugs are visible in the reference screenshot:

BUG 1: PROFILE LOOKUP FALSE-NEGATIVE
- Manifest entry resolves: `prusa_core_one_l` → cover.png + bed.stl + texture.svg load fine.
- Slicer profile API still reports zero machine profiles for this model and triggers the Clone Profiles dialog.
- Suspected cause: name/key mismatch between the manifest printer ID (e.g. `prusa_core_one_l`) and the OrcaSlicer profile lookup key. OrcaSlicer profiles use model names like "Prusa CORE One L 0.4 nozzle" with manufacturer "Prusa". The lookup may be matching on a different field, slug, or normalization.
- Verify: `curl http://orcaslicer-worker:8080/api/profiles | jq '.byHierarchy.Prusa.Models | keys'` — confirm "Prusa_CORE_One_L" or similar key exists. Then trace how the slicer-side machine selector queries that hierarchy.
- Also check: the Clone Profiles dropdown in the screenshot shows Elegoo Centauri (0.2/0.4/0.6/0.8 nozzle) and "qp4-1-Qidi X-Plus 4 0.4 nozzle" — so SOME machine profiles are loaded. Prusa profiles being absent from this dropdown points to either (a) Prusa profiles failing to load entirely, or (b) being filtered out by manufacturer/source.

BUG 2: TEMPLATE SUBSTITUTION FAILURE IN DIALOG TEXT
- Dialog reads: "Clone process profiles from a similar machine to get started quickly with col1."
- "col1" is clearly a placeholder/variable that wasn't replaced with the printer name ("Prusa CORE One L"). Looks like a template literal with the wrong key (e.g., `{column1}` truncated to `col1`, or a default fallback string).
- Find the source of this dialog (likely src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/ — search for "to get started quickly with" or "Clone process profiles").
- Fix the variable interpolation so the actual selected printer name appears.

INVESTIGATION FILES:

- src/orcaslicer-worker/Services/OrcaProfilesService.cs — profile loading and hierarchy

- src/Web/ReactApp/public/assets/orcaslicer/manifest.json — printer ID to asset path mapping (working)

ACCEPTANCE:
- Selecting Prusa CORE One L (and other Prusa CORE One variants) loads its machine profiles without showing the Clone Profiles "no profiles found" dialog.
- If Clone Profiles is needed elsewhere, the dialog text shows the actual printer name instead of "col1".
- Verified across multiple manufacturers (sanity-check Elegoo, Qidi, Bambu, Creality also work).

REFERENCE IMAGE: Clone Profiles dialog screenshot from user 2026-04-26.

The model-id endpoint now gathers all OrcaSlicer aliases and calls ProfilesService.GetMachineProfilesForCatalogModelAsync, which tries each exact alias first and falls back to the worker's manufacturer/model lookup. This addresses Prusa CORE One L cases where assets exist and the profile source can answer by manufacturer/model even if exact alias lookup returns empty. title: Paint mode: drag should paint, not orbit camera (and add Orca paint options)
description:
Two related issues with paint modes (support, color, seam, fuzzy skin):

1) DRAG BEHAVIOR BUG: Clicking and dragging on the model currently does two things at once — it 'fills' a single triangle/face under the cursor AND orbits the camera/bed. Painting should capture the pointer: click on model = begin a paint stroke, drag = freeform paint along the cursor path (continuous brush strokes following the surface), pointer-up = end stroke. Camera orbit/pan must be disabled while a paint mode is active and the pointer is over the canvas. Currently OrbitControls is still receiving the drag.

2) ORCASLICER PARITY OPTIONS: Add the standard OrcaSlicer paint controls. Reference image (Support Painting):
- Tool type selector: 4 icons (Circle/Sphere brush, Fill, Triangle/Bucket fill, [paint mode-specific 4th])
- 'On overhangs only' checkbox (support paint)
- Pen size slider + numeric input (default 1.00)
- Highlight overhangs slider + numeric input (default 37.00°) — support paint specific
- Section view slider + numeric input (clip plane depth)
- Help (?) button
- 'Erase all painting' button

Per-mode tool/option parity should match Orca:
- Support paint: brush, sphere, fill, triangle/bucket; on-overhangs-only; pen size; overhang threshold; section view; clear
- Seam paint: brush, sphere, fill, triangle/bucket; pen size; section view; clear
- Color paint: brush, sphere, fill, triangle/bucket + color picker; pen size; section view; clear
- Fuzzy skin paint: brush, sphere, fill, triangle/bucket; pen size; section view; clear

FILES (likely): src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/components/viewer/SlicerWorkspace.tsx (paint mode state + OrbitControls gating), the four paint overlay components (search for supportPaintMode/colorPaintMode/seamPaintMode/fuzzySkinPaintMode), and the corresponding tool config panels.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Drag on model in any paint mode produces a continuous freeform stroke and does NOT orbit the camera.
- Each paint mode panel exposes the Orca tool selector + pen size + section view + clear, plus mode-specific extras.
notes:
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS (from user 2026-04-25):

3) HIDE BED IN PAINT MODE: When any paint mode is active, hide the print bed (and bed grid/origin marker) entirely — match OrcaSlicer's painting view which shows only the model on a neutral background. Re-show bed when paint mode exits.

4) ORBIT GATING SEMANTICS (refined): Camera orbit/pan should still work in paint mode — but ONLY when the pointer-down hit-tests to empty space (not the model). Specifically:
   - Pointer-down on model → start paint stroke; OrbitControls disabled for the duration of the stroke.
   - Pointer-down on empty canvas (no model raycast hit) → normal orbit/pan behavior.
   - Pointer-up → release the stroke; OrbitControls re-enabled.
   This requires raycasting on pointer-down against the model mesh (not the bed) and conditionally enabling/disabling OrbitControls per-stroke.

Implementation hint: react-three OrbitControls exposes `enabled` and `enableRotate`/`enablePan` props that can be toggled per pointer-down event based on raycast result.

description:
## Architectural Decision

Implement a **hybrid approach** for slicer profile management:

1. **System Profiles** → Served directly by OrcaSlicer worker (read-only)
   - 3000+ filament profiles, 2000+ process profiles from OrcaSlicer disk files
   - Queried incrementally from OrcaSlicer worker API
   - Single source of truth for manufacturer/OrcaFilamentLibrary profiles
   - No duplication in PostgreSQL

2. **Custom Profiles** → Stored in PostgreSQL
   - User-created profiles (new from scratch)
   - User-modified profiles (cloned from system, then customized)
   - User-uploaded profiles (e.g., Micron 180 with no OrcaSlicer support)
   - Marked with `isSystem=false`

## Implementation Plan

### Phase 1: Incremental System Profile Loading (NewSliceJobPage)
- Remove `listHierarchical()` query that loads ALL profiles upfront
- Add incremental queries to OrcaSlicer worker:
  1. User selects printer → `GET /api/profiles/machine/{printerModel}`
  2. User selects machine profile → `POST /api/profiles/filament/for-machines`
  3. Same for process → `POST /api/profiles/process/for-machines`
- Add service methods to `slicerProfilesService.ts` for new endpoints

### Phase 2: Custom Profile Management
- Keep PostgreSQL tables for custom profiles only
- Add `cloneProfile` endpoint to create custom copy from system profile
- Add `uploadProfile` endpoint for user uploads
- UI shows merged view: system profiles (from worker) + custom profiles (from DB)

### Phase 3: Cleanup
- Remove system profile seeding from PostgreSQL (no longer needed)
- Remove duplicate profile data from database
- Update SlicerProfilesPage to use hybrid approach

## API Endpoints

**OrcaSlicer Worker (system profiles):**
- `GET /api/profiles/machine/{printerModel}` - Machine profiles for model
- `POST /api/profiles/filament/for-machines` - Filament for machines
- `POST /api/profiles/process/for-machines` - Process for machines
- `GET /api/profiles/filament/templates` - OrcaFilamentLibrary universals

**API Server (custom profiles):**
- `GET /api/slicer/profiles/custom` - User's custom profiles
- `POST /api/slicer/profiles/clone` - Clone system profile to custom
- `POST /api/slicer/profiles/upload` - Upload custom profile

## Files to Modify

- `src/Web/ReactApp/src/services/slicerProfilesService.ts` - Add incremental methods
- `src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/pages/NewSliceJobPage.tsx` - Use incremental queries
- `src/api/Services/Slicing/ProfilesService.cs` - Custom profile management
- `src/api/Controllers/Slicing/ProfilesController.cs` - Clone/upload endpoints

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] System profiles queried incrementally from OrcaSlicer worker
- [ ] Custom profiles stored in PostgreSQL with isSystem=false
- [ ] Clone workflow: system profile → custom copy in DB
- [ ] Upload workflow: user file → custom profile in DB
- [ ] UI merges both sources for profile selection
- [ ] No duplicate system profiles in PostgreSQL

title: Cut piece Z-placement ignores model rotation

title: Support hollow model cuts (multiple polygon loops)

title: Cut tool only adjusts plane along Z axis (X/Y axis controls non-functional)
description:
The Cut tool UI exposes axis selection (X/Y/Z) and a cut height slider/input, but in practice only the Z axis cut works — selecting X or Y appears to do nothing or still cuts along Z. Expected behavior: when user selects X axis, the cut plane is perpendicular to the X axis and the height/position slider moves the plane along X; same for Y.

INVESTIGATION:
- The plane-position drag handler may be hard-coded to a Z-only convention.
- actualPlanePos may always be derived from the model's Z bounds instead of the active axis bounds.
- The visual plane mesh may not rotate to match the selected axis (or it does, but the splitGeometryAtPlane call still receives a Z-axis worldPlanePos).
- Verify: useFrame quaternion sync, drag delta projection onto cutAxis, and the worldPlanePos passed to splitGeometryAtPlane all respect cutAxis.

Files: src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/components/viewer/CutPlaneOverlay.tsx (drag handlers, useFrame, handleConfirm). The CutOptions type already carries cutAxis + worldPlanePos, so the data path supports it; the UI/interaction wiring needs to be verified end-to-end.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Selecting X axis lets user drag/type a cut position along X; the visual plane is perpendicular to X; confirming produces +X / -X pieces.
- Same for Y.
- Z continues to work as it does today.

title: Cut piece Z-placement ignores model rotation
description: computePieceZ in SlicerWorkspace.tsx derives Z from -minZ * (sz - 1) using only the Z-scale component. If a model was rotated before cutting (e.g., via lay-flat or manual rotation), the cut pieces inherit that rotation but Z-placement won't account for it — the lowest rotated vertex may not correspond to min.z of the geometry. The correct formula (as in computeZForBedPlacement) should iterate all vertices with rotation applied. Acceptable for v1 since 3D print models typically sit flat. From Kane's code review of commit 45585a44.
notes: Already implemented in commit 45585a44. computeBedZ in handleCutComplete (SlicerWorkspace.tsx:868-880) iterates all geometry vertices applying parentQuat (quaternion derived from parentRotation) and parentScaleVec, then uses min rotated Z for bed placement — exactly matching computeZForBedPlacement. The pre-fix scale-only formula no longer exists.

- Upserts based on ExternalId first, then ManufacturerName + FilamentName
- Returns import summary: created count, updated count, error count, error details

## Goal

Implement custom profile management where users can clone system profiles or upload their own.

## Use Cases

1. **Clone & Customize**: User takes a system profile (e.g., 'Generic ABS @Ratrig') and modifies settings

```csharp
// Clone a system profile to create a custom copy
POST /api/slicer/profiles/clone
Body: { sourceProfileId: string, sourceType: 'machine'|'filament'|'process', name: string }
Returns: CustomProfileDto

// Upload a custom profile
POST /api/slicer/profiles/upload
Body: { rawJson: string, profileType: 'machine'|'filament'|'process', name: string }
Returns: CustomProfileDto

// List user's custom profiles
GET /api/slicer/profiles/custom
Returns: CustomProfileDto[]

// Update custom profile
PUT /api/slicer/profiles/custom/{id}
Body: { rawJson: string, name: string }

// Delete custom profile
DELETE /api/slicer/profiles/custom/{id}
```

- ProcessProfile

```typescript
async listCustomProfiles(): Promise<CustomProfile[]>
async updateCustomProfile(id: string, data: Partial<CustomProfile>): Promise<CustomProfile>

```

title: Epic: OrcaSlicer Profile Selection Flow Redesign
description:
## Overview
The slicer panel profile selection flow is fundamentally broken. The current implementation uses printer instances instead of printer models, hardcodes filament profiles, and shows worker versions instead of slicer types.

## Required Flow (OrcaSlicer-style)
1. **Printer Model** → User selects from catalog (/api/catalog/printer-models)
2. **Machine Profiles** → Populated based on selected printer model (with nozzle variants)
3. **Filament Profiles** → Filtered by selected machine profile (from API, not hardcoded)
4. **Process Profiles** → Filtered by selected machine profile (from API)
5. **Slicer Selection** → Shows slicer types/versions (OrcaSlicer, PrusaSlicer), not worker info

## Current Problems
| Component | Current | Required |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| Printer Selection | selectedPrinterId (instances) | Printer Model from catalog |
| Machine Profiles | Not shown, flat list | Dropdown filtered by printer model |
| Filament Profiles | Hardcoded MATERIAL_PRESETS | API-driven, filtered by machine |
| Process Profiles | Returns ALL profiles | Filtered by machine profile |
| Slicer Selection | Worker versions | Slicer types/versions |

## API Support Available
- /api/catalog/printer-models - printer models with specs
- /api/slicer/profiles/hierarchy?machineProfileId=X - filtered profiles
- byHierarchy[manufacturer].models[model] structure exists

## Files to Modify
- src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/pages/NewSliceJobPage.tsx
- src/Web/ReactApp/src/services/slicerProfilesService.ts
- Possibly: src/Web/ReactApp/src/features/slicer/components/ProfileSelector.tsx

- [ ] No hardcoded material presets
- [ ] Slicer dropdown shows types, not worker info
- [ ] All profiles come from API
- [ ] UI matches OrcaSlicer-style workflow
